summary: The note explains why sportsmanship matters on amateur sports teams, defining it as fair play, rule-following, and respect for opponents and officials. It covers its effects on team dynamics, player development and long-term life skills, and how local teams, coaches, parents and leagues promote and reward it. It also addresses handling poor sportsmanship and includes an FAQ, set against a surge in amateur participation after social restrictions eased on September 10, 2023.
one_line: Sportsmanship in amateur sports builds positive team culture, player growth and lifelong skills, supported by coaches, parents, workshops, awards and constructive handling of misconduct.
key_facts: Participation in amateur sports teams surged after social restrictions eased on September 10, 2023.

Sportsmanship is defined as playing fair, following the rules, and respecting the judgment of referees and officials, including fair play, respect for opponents, and gracious behavior in winning or losing.
On October 5, 2023, Riverside Hawks basketball coach Michael Thompson said teaching sportsmanship fosters 'a spirit of camaraderie and mutual respect' that is the backbone of team culture.

Developmental psychologist Dr. Hannah Lee, interviewed on November 14, 2023, said sportsmanship can 'positively influence a player's emotional and social growth by instilling discipline, empathy, and resilience.'

On September 20, 2023, the Valley Soccer Club began sportsmanship workshops led by former professional soccer player David Rodriguez, covering team building, conflict resolution, and respect in competition.
Lisa Chang of the Maplewood Tennis Association emphasizes the 'Coaches Creed' to her staff, stressing respect, humility, and integrity.
Parents are encouraged to support teams positively, respect officials' decisions, and behave respectfully toward spectators, teams, and coaches.

Corporate executive and former amateur football player Jameson Clark said on December 1, 2023 that his sports experience taught him to cooperate with diverse personalities and handle project highs and lows.
On October 25, 2023, the Wildwood Basketball League established a 'Sportsmanship of the Year' award nominated by peers, coaches, and fans.
During a local high school soccer match on September 15, 2023, players from both teams jointly halted play when an opposing player was injured.
Poor sportsmanship should be addressed through codes of conduct and constructive feedback rather than punitive measures, treating incidents as teachable moments.
The FAQ states sportsmanship is a higher priority than winning, is compatible with competitiveness, and may boost morale and team unity, potentially improving performance.
